sentiment.rationale: Management explicitly raised forward revenue guidance for 2026 to 'low-double digits' with an ambition to grow even faster, and Q1 2026 revenue guidance of 14-16% growth represents a clear acceleration from Q4 2025's 12% growth. The guidance raise is organic, driven by product initiatives (Reserve Now, Pay Later, simplified fees, Project Y) and not primarily attributed to FX or one-time items. Management language is confident and forward-looking, with no material risks or hedges raised in Q&A.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue of $2.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
summary.eps: Not disclosed (net income of $341 million was reported, but EPS not explicitly stated).
summary.guidance: Q1 2026 revenue expected to be $2.59 billion to $2.63 billion, representing 14% to 16% year-over-year growth. Full-year 2026 revenue growth expected to accelerate to low-double digits, with ambition to grow even faster. Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be stable year-over-year.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin of 28%. Full-year 2025 free cash flow margin of 38%. 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be stable year-over-year.
key_risks: Travel is influenced by currency, macroeconomic conditions, and global events, which cannot be predicted with precision.
FX tailwinds expected to fade as 2026 progresses.
Cancellation rates increased by approximately 1% due to Reserve Now, Pay Later (from ~16% to ~17%).
key_opportunities: Project Y expected to deliver hundreds of millions more in revenue in 2026.
Pricing initiatives (Reserve Now, Pay Later, simplified fees) expected to drive as much revenue as Project Y in 2026.
Expansion into new markets (Brazil, India, Japan) showing strong growth.
Major events (2026 FIFA World Cup, Milan Olympics) expected to drive supply and brand awareness.
AI initiatives (customer service, AI search) expected to improve efficiency and user experience.
Hotel expansion (boutique and independent hotels) represents a massive opportunity.
Services/experiences (grocery delivery, airport pickups) being tested to capture more of the trip.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Brian Chesky stated 'we're seeing increased momentum' and 'the opportunity ahead is even bigger than what you're seeing today,' reflecting strong confidence in the forward outlook.

evidence.claim: Q4 2025 revenue was $2.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
evidence.quote: Revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $2.8 billion, exceeding the high end of our guidance.

evidence.claim: Q1 2026 revenue guidance is $2.59 billion to $2.63 billion, representing 14% to 16% year-over-year growth.
evidence.quote: In Q1, we expect to generate revenue of $2.59 billion to $2.63 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 14% to 16%.

evidence.claim: Full-year 2026 revenue growth expected to accelerate to low-double digits, with ambition to grow even faster.
evidence.quote: For the full year 2026, we expect year-over-year revenue growth to accelerate to low-double digits, with an ambition to grow even faster than that.

evidence.claim: 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be stable year-over-year.
evidence.quote: We expect our 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin to be stable year-over-year.
We generated $786 million of adjusted EBITDA, representing a 28% adjusted EBITDA margin, also exceeding guidance.

evidence.claim: Full-year 2025 free cash flow margin was 38%.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we generated $4.6 billion, representing a free cash flow margin of 38%.

evidence.claim: Net income was $341 million, but EPS not disclosed.
evidence.quote: Finally, net income was $341 million and was negatively impacted by roughly $90 million of onetime non-income tax.

evidence.claim: Project Y expected to deliver hundreds of millions more in revenue in 2026.
evidence.quote: And we believe Project Y will deliver hundreds of millions more this year.

evidence.claim: Pricing initiatives expected to drive as much revenue as Project Y in 2026.
evidence.quote: Now we believe that pricing initiatives will drive as much revenue this year as Y and will remain a strong tailwind for years to come.

evidence.claim: Brazil moved from a top 10 to a top 5 market; Q4 was second largest contributor to first-time bookers.
evidence.quote: Brazil moved from a top 10 market to a top five market on Airbnb. In Q4, it was our second largest contributor to first-time bookers, behind only the US.

evidence.claim: Major events (World Cup, Olympics) are expected to drive supply and brand awareness.
evidence.quote: We're also excited about major events this year, including the Winter Olympics happening now in Milan and the FIFA World Cup coming this summer.

evidence.claim: AI customer service agent resolving a third of support issues; rollout to global planned.
evidence.quote: It's already resolving a third of the support issues without needing a live specialist, and resolution times are significantly faster. It's live across North America, and we're planning to roll it out globally.

evidence.claim: Hotel expansion represents a massive opportunity; hotels growing nearly double the platform rate.
evidence.quote: Hotels was a single-digit percentage of total nights booked, but growing nearly double that of the overall platform.

evidence.claim: Cancellation rates increased by approximately 1% due to Reserve Now, Pay Later.
evidence.quote: One piece of perspective is that, in terms of the aggregate nominal increase in cancellations rate, it's approximately 1%, so an average of maybe 16% cancellation rates historically going to 17%.

evidence.claim: FX tailwinds expected to fade as 2026 progresses.
evidence.quote: While FX tailwinds should fade as the year progresses, we're encouraged by healthy demand and execution across our growth initiatives.
We're seeing increased momentum. That doesn't happen by accident. It's a result of an incredible team rowing in the same direction at global scale.

evidence.claim: Guidance raise is organic, not primarily attributed to FX or one-time items.
evidence.quote: We expect revenue growth to accelerate to at least low-double digits in 2026. We expect adjusted EBITDA margin to be stable year-over-year. And we'll do all of this without investing billions or tens of billions of dollars.
